SK2083 The collection iterated here is provably empty

A local collection is created empty, is never referred to except as the subject of a foreach, and is then iterated — so the loop body cannot run.

CategoryCorrectness
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since1.3
SupersedesS4158

Why

The population step was removed, or was never written. The loop reads as working code, the compiler has nothing to say about it, and every test over it passes, because a body that never runs never fails. The repair is the missing step, which is why there is no fix: deleting the loop would silence the rule and keep the defect.

Example

Instead of:

var overdue = new List<Invoice>();
foreach (var invoice in overdue) {
    Remind(invoice);
}

Write:

var overdue = new List<Invoice>();
overdue.AddRange(invoices.Where(static i => i.IsOverdue));
foreach (var invoice in overdue) {
    Remind(invoice);
}

When it does not fire

⚠ This is proved by exhaustion, not by dataflow. Roslyn's AnalyzeDataFlow answers questions about variables and not about a collection's contents, so the rule asks a question it can answer instead: every reference to the local inside the member that declares it must be the subject of a foreach. A collection can only be filled through a member call, an assignment, or by being handed somewhere, and each of those is a reference that is not a foreach subject — so one reference of any other kind, including an argument, a receiver, an assignment target, a ref or a capture, withdraws the finding, and the analyzer never has to decide what that reference does. ⚠ The scan runs over the whole enclosing member rather than forward from the declaration. A lambda or local function declared before the local cannot capture it, and one declared after it holds a reference the scan sees, so the answer does not depend on ordering — which is what makes the exhaustion argument sound. ⚠ Locals only. A field or a property can be filled by any member of the type and by anything holding the instance, so "nothing adds to it" is not a claim available there. The initialiser must be an empty collection expression, an empty array, Array.Empty<T>(), Enumerable.Empty<T>(), or a parameterless construction of a known framework collection; any constructor argument withdraws it, because a capacity leaves the collection empty and a source collection does not, and declining both is cheaper than telling them apart. foreach over something that is not a plain name — an expression, a call, a member path — is not examined at all.
